title: Quatre-quarts
subtitle: The French pound cake where all four ingredients weigh exactly the same
excerpt: Quatre-quarts means four quarters: eggs, butter, flour, and sugar in equal weight. A standard egg weighs about 60 g, so weigh the eggs first and use that weight for the other three. The result is a dense, golden, buttery cake that keeps for several days and forms the base of many French pastry preparations.
sourceNotes: Quatre-quarts is the French equivalent of the British pound cake and the American one-two-three-four cake. The equal-weight ratio is the same across all three traditions. The French version is associated with Brittany, where it is baked as a loaf or in a round tin. The recipe has been documented in French household cookbooks since at least the nineteenth century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice and freeze. Thaw at room temperature for 1 hour.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps well for 4 to 5 days wrapped in baking paper at room temperature. Flavour improves on day two.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 170 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 155 degrees Celsius. Middle shelf.

glossaryTerms.definition: The equal-weight ratio at the heart of the French pound cake: equal parts eggs, butter, flour, and sugar. Weigh the eggs first (shells off) and use that weight for each of the other three ingredients. Four large eggs weigh roughly 240 g, which gives a generous loaf.

content.text: means you do not need to look up a recipe. Weigh the eggs, and that number is your guide for everything else. Creaming the butter and sugar properly is the only technique that matters here; skip it and the cake will be dense rather than tender.

items.prepNote: weighed without shells; this weight determines all other quantities

content.text: Preheat the oven to 170 degrees Celsius. Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin or a 20 cm round cake tin.
Beat the butter and sugar together for 5 to 6 minutes until very pale and fluffy. Add the vanilla and lemon zest.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each. If the batter looks curdled, add a tablespoon of flour and continue.
Sift in the flour, baking powder, and salt. Fold in gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour into the tin. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes (loaf) or 30 to 35 minutes (round) until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.

Replace 30 g of flour with cocoa powder for a chocolate version. Add the zest of 2 oranges and a tablespoon of Grand Marnier for an orange cake. Replace the vanilla with almond extract and scatter flaked almonds on top before baking. The base ratio stays the same.
